body.estimand_functional:
The causal target remains
\(\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\mathbb E[B_{si}(1)-B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]\).
Consistency and event-date transport imply, rather than define, its equality
with the observed-law functional \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)\).
For each fixed admissible query, random-design risk, coverage, and expected
length are stated uniformly over the labelled conditional-kernel class
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), and the minimax decision rule is one
data-measurable rule chosen before taking the supremum over query values.
The deterministic fixed-design experiment has minimax mean squared error
\(\asymp R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\) under the stated converse slack and admits the
nearest-design upper witness for every fixed design.  For
\(0<\lambda\le1\), the anchor estimator has marginal squared risk at most
\(CR_\star\), and the unit-history interval is uniformly conditionally
honest with expected length at most \(CR_\star^{1/2}\); the matching
fixed-query-kernel converses hold under the stated strict interior and donor
moment slack.  Separately, for every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), its
labelled regular conditional kernel belongs to
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) for almost every query under the marginal
law of \(z_0\), and the kernel conclusions transfer there with
\(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau\).  No supremum over law-specific null
conditional versions is taken.  No headline result assumes a lower local
modulus, and no claim is made for \(\lambda>1\).

sampling_model.design: For each cohort, date, and almost every realized query \(z_0\), the exact pre-event path has a conditional density between \(c_X\) and \(C_X\).  Given \(z_0\), each cohort's design sequence is geometrically beta mixing.  The conditionally independent-calendar subclass requires independence only of the design dates given \(z_0\).  Conditional analysis itself is carried out in the separately defined deterministic experiment for every fixed design; the Gram radius is an upper certificate and never a converse.
sampling_model.units: Each cohort supplies \(n_s\) replicated untreated blocks per date and \(n_s\) treated event outcomes.  Given the exact design and realized query, unit histories are independent across units and have the stated conditional means.  Dependence across all training dates and the event outcome within one unit history remains unrestricted; inference treats that whole history as one bounded observation.
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency identifies observed event wealth with treated potential wealth.  Event-date transport separately equates the unobserved untreated event mean with the historical regression at the realized path; query-conditional design regularity and design-conditional centering do not establish this causal equality.
sampling_model.overlap: Every realized cohort path is at least \(\delta_0\) from the cube boundary.  Exact fixed-design recovery can be easier than an anchor bandwidth suggests when a site equals the realized path.  The regular donor-location converse requires \(\delta_0<1/2\), because the admissible displacement can otherwise collapse.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the event query is generated: deterministic donor folds produce projected means, and the full stacked covariance retains cross-coordinate, cross-horizon, and cross-cohort dependence.  Conditional on the realized query, donors are independent of the entire joint design-response-event panel, so further design conditioning preserves donor independence from unit histories.  For \(0<\lambda\le1\), local-constant weights are nonnegative with unit absolute mass; this makes whole-unit concentration sufficient and avoids both deconvolution and calendar-score studentization.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Gaussian convex-class theory links linear-functional minimax risk to a known-experiment modulus; it does not supply the bounded replicated-response and generated-query product experiment used here.
Its estimated-minimizer results use sample splitting and strong convexity, making location error second order rather than a rough-Holder external-query modulus.
Its generated-covariate expansion attaches an estimated coordinate to every training row, unlike the exact historical design and generated event query here.
Its replicated errors-in-variables experiment contaminates every latent training coordinate and requires deconvolution, which is absent under center-only generation.
The classical random-design Holder benchmark supplies ordinary smoothing context but not query-conditional spacing or a generated donor center.
Pointwise local-polynomial minimax theory motivates the anchor smoother but not the bounded product-experiment nearest-site frontier.
Optimal local-polynomial kernels concern ordinary pointwise asymptotic efficiency; the present result establishes only rate constants for a generated-query product experiment.
Random-design sup-norm sharp estimation addresses global loss and design adaptation, not conditional nearest-site recovery at an external generated query.
Classical nonparametric errors-in-variables contaminates all regression covariates, so its deconvolution rates do not govern the center-only design used here.
Generated-regressor asymptotic variance uses smooth semiparametric expansions; it does not cover the nonsmooth rough-Holder query modulus or its minimax converse.
Honest confidence-interval adaptation impossibility motivates fixing the Holder radius and smoothness rather than claiming adaptation across classes.
Ordered moduli characterize confidence intervals for linear functionals in known Gaussian experiments; the current interval must additionally cover generated-center error.
Bias-aware ordinary-regression intervals combine worst-case bias and stochastic calibration but contain no external full-covariance donor query.
Dependent-data resampling is not invoked: the repaired theorem uses whole-unit bounded-range concentration and design mixing only for anchor occupancy.
Many-control panel asymptotics motivate cross-unit replication but do not provide the generated-query optimal-recovery frontier.
Dependent synthetic-control prediction intervals address dependent innovations and estimated weights; the repaired interval instead uses unit-history concentration and no calendar-block calibration.
Conformal synthetic-control inference targets robust prediction coverage under a different exchangeability/time-series architecture, not full-covariance generated-query expected-length minimaxity.
The synthetic-control review motivates consistency and data-architecture transparency but does not validate the event-date counterfactual transport equality used for causal identification.
The longitudinal and panel causal-model survey locates the identifying assumptions; it does not derive the conditional generated-proxy minimax or honest-length frontier.

body.tldr: The paper now delivers a sharp rate frontier only for the rough Holder regime \(0<\lambda\le1\), where \(\kappa=\lambda\).  Consistency and the explicitly untestable event-date transport equality identify the cohort-weighted buy-and-hold contrast.  Conditional on the realized query, the donor sample factors from the complete joint panel, while every design date has a uniformly bounded conditional density and each cohort's design sequence is conditionally geometrically beta mixing.  These query-conditional design conditions prevent an event path from selecting a largest design hole.  A deterministic fixed-design product modulus gives the conditional frontier; marginally, the nonredundant channels are treated replication, query-conditional calendar spacing, and donor location.  The feasible interval uses bounded concentration across independent unit histories only, with no calendar-score branch.  Conditional design independence removes the geometric-mixing logarithm.  Higher-order signed-weight stability for \(\lambda>1\) and exact phase-intersection constants remain open.

project_justification.gap: Classical fixed-point regression does not combine replicated sites with an external full-covariance generated query, and unconditional design regularity does not control occupancy after conditioning on a design-dependent realized query.  Existing ordinary-regression and synthetic-control intervals also do not justify treating globally design-selected calendar scores as independent blocks.
project_justification.niche: Historical paths can be recorded exactly while only the event-date counterfactual path is synthesized from donors.  In the rough Holder regime this separates exact-design optimal recovery, query-conditional spacing, full-covariance donor-location uncertainty, and the untestable causal transport equality.
project_justification.fill: The note imposes explicit query-conditional density and design-mixing conditions, defines a deterministic bounded product experiment and joint modulus, and proves conditional, marginal, and honest-length rate frontiers for \(0<\lambda\le1\).  A nearest-site rule and an anchor/extrapolation rule attain the risk rates.  The honest interval uses whole-unit bounded-range concentration, generated-center bias calibration, and total fallbacks; its matching lower bounds use explicit treated, spacing, and arbitrarily overlapping full-covariance donor pairs.

body.related_work: Donoho (1994) relates a linear-functional modulus to minimax recovery in a known Gaussian convex experiment; the conditional theorem instead constructs a bounded \((E,Q,Z)\) product experiment with an external full-covariance query, a nearest-site characterization, and an almost-sure causal bridge.  Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) evaluate at an independently estimated minimizer under strong convexity, which makes center error second order and does not yield the rough-Holder donor channel.  Stone (1982), Fan (1993), Fan et al. (1997), and Gaiffas (2007) provide ordinary Holder, pointwise local-polynomial, kernel-efficiency, and random-design sup-norm benchmarks, respectively; none combines query-conditional spacing with replicated unit histories and a generated event center.  Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012), Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008), and Fan and Truong (1993) perturb every training coordinate, unlike the exact historical design here; Hahn and Ridder (2013) give smooth generated-regressor variance expansions rather than a nonsmooth minimax modulus.  For inference, Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) supply ordered-modulus and bias-aware ordinary-regression benchmarks, and Low (1997) explains why adaptation is not claimed.  Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021), Kunsch (1989), and Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu (2021) concern dependent synthetic-control prediction, resampling, or conformal architectures; none is used to justify calendar-block calibration in the repaired interval, which instead concentrates independent whole-unit histories.  Ferman (2021) motivates many-control replication.  Abadie (2021) and Arkhangelsky and Imbens (2024) frame consistency and panel causal assumptions but do not validate event-date transport or derive the statistical frontier.
body.interpretation: Conditionally, exact-site geometry and a generated donor query are separate sources of difficulty.  Query-conditional density and design mixing ensure that a realized event path cannot systematically select an unregulated design hole, so occupancy converts fixed-design ambiguity into the geometric-mixing spacing rate.  Donor uncertainty dominates when \(N^{-\lambda}\) exceeds treated replication and spacing.  The inference result does not require calendar response mixing: it conditions on the selected design and donors and concentrates across independent unit histories, preserving arbitrary response dependence over time within a unit.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The no-deconvolution conclusion relies on exact historical paths, and every constructive headline is restricted to \(0<\lambda\le1\).  For \(\lambda>1\), higher-order fixed-design recovery uses signed weights whose conditional stochastic norm is not controlled by the present assumptions.  Geometric conditional design mixing retains the logarithmic spacing penalty; only conditional design independence yields the no-log term.  The donor converse requires \(B^4>(Sd)^2\) and \(\delta_0<1/2\).  The unit-history interval is rate-optimal but conservative, and exact phase-intersection constants remain open.
body.honest_scope: Event-date transport is an untestable causal restriction.  Query-conditional density and design mixing are observed-law design restrictions, while design-conditional centering is a separate response sampling condition.  Donor-panel separation factors donors from the complete joint panel conditional on the query and leaves dependence within each unit's training-event history unrestricted.  Risk, coverage, and expected-length upper bounds hold over the base rough-Holder class without a lower local modulus.  The interval uses no calendar-score branch or estimated-variance division.  The donor converse needs strict interior and fourth-moment slack.  Higher smoothness, growing dimension, adaptation, uniform-in-query bands, and exact constants are outside scope.
